correctness.rationale: Condition on shared P: with n=d-|S|-2 unvaccinated other leaves, second vaccination difference equals -E[P^2(Pr(Bin(n,P)=r-2)-Pr(Bin(n,P)=r-1))]. Beta integration gives A_n and C_n with ratio C_n/A_n=((n-r+2)/(r-1))*((alpha+r)/(beta+n-r+1)). The resulting condition L(n)>=(0) is affine decreasing slope -(alpha+1), hence worst at n=d-2 and exactly reduces to (r-1)beta-(d-r)alpha >= d-1. For n=r-2 the sign is strictly negative, for n<r-2 zero. At r=1 the sign is positive for all pair choices; at r=d it is nonpositive. Independent exact rational Beta moments reconstruct for d=5,r=3,mu=1/4: correlation rho=1/6,1/5,1/3 gives respectively second differences -195/57344,0,3/256 and criterion lhs 1,0,-2, confirming strict sign reversal at the predicted boundary. Interpolating real parameters is justified algebraically by positivity of Gamma/Beta moments, not by finite grids.

value.rationale: An exact necessary-and-sufficient correlation threshold for diminishing vaccine returns is a motivated structural property of a natural exchangeable outbreak model. It quantifies a genuine sign flip even at constant expected infections prevented, rather than just an expected-case modularity calculation.
residual_risks: Only one-generation stars, homogeneous leaves, pre-exposure perfect vaccination, Beta common-risk mixture; no causal population-level vaccine efficacy claims.

final_claim: For a single-infectiousness Beta(alpha,beta) mixture with homogeneous leaf exposures, outbreak-overload vaccination benefit on a d-leaf star is submodular iff r=d or (2<=r<=d-1 and (r-1)beta-(d-r)alpha>=d-1), and never when r=1; equivalently correlation/mean condition mu+rho/(1-rho)<=(r-1)/(d-1).
